title: Sitemap discovery and recursive parsing engine

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 STATIC AUDIT — SPRINT 3 — ROUND 1 — VERDICT: CONDITIONAL
Audited commit 786dcb5 on branch devteam2/sprint-3 in worktree ../content-checker-devteam2-sprint-3, diffed against merge-base 11bca26 (Sprint 1 close). Worktree clean; committed code. Lifecycle state for this sprint lives on the worktree branch (started there), so this verdict is recorded from the worktree.
Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. No cross-version ("arrives between release A and B") criterion in this sprint.
Ownership boundary held: diff touches only lib/sitemap/, test/sitemap/, test/fixtures/sitemap/ (27 fixtures), package.json, package-lock.json, and lifecycle bookkeeping. Nothing in src/. One new dependency (fast-xml-parser 5.11.1, plus its transitive deps in the lockfile).

Most of this module is good work. The engine's shape — typed errors, injectable fetch/DNS, include-when-unsure classification, fixture-driven tests that assert on counts and request sequence — is what the sprint asked for and it's built carefully. The findings below are real, demonstrated, and mostly small; one of them is a requirement not met.

=== REQUIRED FIXES (the CONDITIONAL) ===

A. [HIGH — requirement 8 not met] The overall operation budget is only checked at admission; queued and in-flight work never re-checks it. lib/sitemap/crawl.js:46-49.
   The budget check runs once per visitSitemap() call, synchronously, before the fetch is queued behind the concurrency limiter. Every sibling child of an index is admitted in the same tick at t≈0, so for a flat index (Yoast's normal shape) the budget can never trip after that — however long the queue takes.
   DEMONSTRATED: 10-child flat index, concurrency 1, 30ms per child, budgetMs 50 → all 10 children fetched, 319ms elapsed, truncated:false. The budget was exceeded 6x and the result says it wasn't.
   On the sprint's own headline case (2,057-child index): cap admits 50 at t≈0, concurrency 5, slow server hitting the 15s per-request timeout → 50/5 × 15s = 150s against a 90s budget, and truncated only reflects the cap. Discovery is also un-budgeted (robots.txt + up to N declared + 3 candidates, each up to 15s) and can consume the whole budget before the crawl starts — it then trips immediately at the first visit, which is at least honest, but the crawl-phase gap is not.
   The existing test (crawl.test.js:159) proves the budget only for a sequential chain and its own comment says why: "sibling children ... are all budget-checked near-simultaneously." That's the gap, named in the test, not closed.
   Acceptance criterion says QA1 confirms "the per-request and overall timeouts are both enforced." The overall one is not, for the common shape.
   FIX SHAPE (Dev Team's call how): re-check the budget inside the limiter callback immediately before the fetch actually starts (so queued work is dropped, recorded in skipped, and truncated set), and/or drive one budget-wide AbortController that in-flight fetches also observe. Add a flat-index budget test alongside the sequential one.

B. [MEDIUM — requirement 8 text] The root document counts against the CHILD cap. crawl.js:50-54. A pre-parsed root (preParsedDoc set) still increments fetchedCount, so maxChildren:50 fetches 49 children.
   DEMONSTRATED: maxChildren:1 → zero child sitemaps fetched, truncated:true, urls:[]. A cap of "1 child sitemap" fetched no child sitemaps.
   Dev Team knows — crawl.test.js:151 comment: "maxChildren: 4 // root + 3 children before the cap trips." The requirement says "cap the number of child sitemaps fetched." Don't count a root that was never fetched here.

C. [MEDIUM — requirement 6] Truncated children vanish from the result; ambiguous is flagged for children that were never visited. crawl.js:46-53, :91-94.
   When the cap or budget trips, visitSitemap returns without recording the child anywhere — not in skipped, not in consulted. Requirement 6: "the result must carry the list of sitemaps consulted and any that were skipped ... so callers can surface it." A caller gets truncated:true but cannot say which sitemaps were cut. Meanwhile the ambiguous flag is pushed BEFORE the visit (crawl.js:92), so a child that was classified ambiguous and then truncated appears in ambiguous ("included, check it") while never having been fetched.
   DEMONSTRATED: 2-child index, maxChildren:2 (so 1 child after B's off-by-one) → ambiguous lists both children; consulted lists one. Sprint 5's UI would tell the developer "news-sitemap.xml was included but unsure" when it was not included at all.
   FIX: push {url, reason:'truncated:cap'|'truncated:budget'} to skipped when the check trips; move the ambiguous push to after the visit succeeds (or key it off consulted).

D. [MEDIUM — same defect class as Sprint 2's CONDITIONAL, one week ago] Two SSRF-path bugs that mask each other. lib/sitemap/ssrf.js:89 and httpClient.js:70.
   (i) extractIPv4MappedAddress matches only the dotted spelling (/^::ffff:(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)$/). isDisallowedAddress('::ffff:7f00:1', 6) → ALLOW. isDisallowedAddress('::ffff:c0a8:10a', 6) → ALLOW. Same regex, same hole, that I failed Sprint 2 on; Sprint 2's fix (net.BlockList, which checks the address's value in either spelling — verified again here: BlockList.check('::ffff:7f00:1','ipv6') → true) is on main now.
   (ii) httpClient passes new URL().hostname to dns.lookup unchanged, and for an IPv6 literal that hostname is BRACKETED ("[::1]"). Real dns.promises.lookup('[::1]') throws ENOTFOUND. So every IPv6-literal URL fails as DNS_ERROR — including a legitimate http://[2001:db8::1]/ (DEMONSTRATED with a fake resolver that would have answered), and http://[::1]/ is refused with the wrong type (DNS_ERROR, not SSRF_BLOCKED — a requirement 11 typing error).
   Why this is CONDITIONAL and not FAIL on its own: (ii) currently blocks every literal that could reach (i), and this platform's resolver renders a real AAAA mapped record in dotted form (verified via inet_ntop: '::ffff:7f00:1' → '::ffff:127.0.0.1'), so the hex hole is latent, not live, today. It goes live the moment someone fixes (ii) without (i) — which is exactly what a "fix IPv6 literals" ticket would do. Fix both together, now, while the Sprint 2 precedent is fresh: strip brackets before lookup, replace the hand-rolled range checks with net.BlockList (keep the fe80::/10, fc00::/7, 0.0.0.0/8 and :: additions — those are correct and go beyond Sprint 2's list, which is fine). Add a test that goes through guardedFetch with a bracketed literal in both spellings.

E. [MEDIUM — requirement 11 typing, under-collection direction] Content-Type vetoes a valid sitemap body. lib/sitemap/xml.js:37-41.
   The module comment (xml.js:28-29) says "the body's actual shape is always the deciding factor, since servers frequently mislabel it." The code says the opposite: contentTypeSaysHtml alone throws NonXmlResponseError before the body is examined.
   DEMONSTRATED: a valid <urlset> body with contentType 'text/html; charset=UTF-8' → NON_XML_RESPONSE. That is a wrong type (the body IS XML) and it drops a good sitemap because a server default was misconfigured — the under-collection direction the sprint calls its highest-severity risk. It is visible (skipped / attempt log), not silent, which is why this isn't a FAIL by itself; but comment and code contradicting each other means nobody re-read this after writing it.
   FIX: let the body decide. Use content-type only as a tiebreaker when the body doesn't parse, or drop the veto. Keep the looksLikeHtml body sniff.

=== REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE ===
1. Standalone module, no routes/UI — MET. lib/sitemap/index.js exports discoverAndParseSitemap; no express import anywhere in lib/sitemap; no require() reaching into src/. index.test.js:95 asserts it.
2. Discovery order robots.txt → candidates → typed failure — MET, asserted on request sequence (discovery.test.js:26: robots.txt, then /sitemap_index.xml, then /wp-sitemap.xml). Every Sitemap: directive is used; falls through to candidates when all declared ones fail to validate; SitemapDiscoveryFailedError carries the full attempt log.
3. Manual URL bypasses discovery — MET. index.js:104-108; failure propagates typed with no fallback.
4. Recursion ≥3 deep with cycle detection — MET. visited-set keyed on normalized href; cyclic and self-referencing fixtures terminate (crawl.test.js:84, :99); depth-3 nested fixture resolves fully (:73). Safety depth 20 is a valve, not a limit — acceptable and documented.
5. Filename-agnostic child selection — MET. Token-based classifier handles page-sitemap.xml, post-sitemap2.xml, sitemap-page-1.xml, wp-sitemap-posts-post-1.xml. Exclusion list covers product/category/author/tag/media/attachment plus taxonomy/user. See non-blocking G for a startsWith concern.
6. Include-when-unsure + consulted/skipped/ambiguous lists — PARTIALLY MET. Unrecognized children are included and flagged (yoast fixture: gallery-sitemap included, urls.size 7 asserted). Lists are present in the result shape. But truncated children are recorded nowhere and ambiguous can list unvisited children — finding C.
7. Basic auth on every request in chain to same host; consume Sprint 2's decrypt helper — MET, with a ruling (see Q&A). Authorization asserted on both child requests in crawl.test.js:205; forwarded on same-host redirect, dropped on cross-host (httpClient.test.js:138, :152). No logging anywhere in lib/sitemap; auth never attached to an error or result object.
8. Per-request timeout, overall budget, child cap with truncated flag — PARTIALLY MET. Per-request timeout: enforced across the whole redirect chain via one AbortController, tested. Cap: enforced, truncated set, tested — but off by one (B). Budget: NOT enforced for queued siblings (A).
9. Concurrency limit + descriptive User-Agent — MET. Hand-rolled limiter is 42 lines, correct, tested; UA 'ContentCheckerBot/1.0 (+https://tools.wordzite.com/content-check)'.
10. Request-time SSRF after DNS and after every redirect — MET as written (assertHostIsSafe runs at the top of every hop, tested at httpClient.test.js:165), with the latent defect in D and the TOCTOU note in F.
11. Typed distinguishable failures — MET, except the two mis-typings in D(ii) and E. DNS_ERROR / CONNECTION_ERROR / TIMEOUT / HTTP_401 / HTTP_403 / HTTP_404 / HTTP_ERROR / NON_XML_RESPONSE / MALFORMED_XML / SSRF_BLOCKED / TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS / DISCOVERY_FAILED, each its own class with a stable .code. 401 vs 404 asserted distinguishable (httpClient.test.js:65).
12. Namespaced docs, XML declaration, xml-stylesheet PI, image: children, loc + lastmod — MET. fast-xml-parser with removeNSPrefix/ignoreDeclaration/ignorePiTags; the empty-urlset '' quirk was caught by their own test and handled with an 'in' check, which is the right fix.
13. Fixture-only tests covering the nine named scenarios — MET, and I verified the no-network claim the hard way: ran all 100 sitemap tests with dns.lookup, dns.promises.lookup, resolve4/6 and global fetch replaced by functions that throw. 100/100 pass. Full suite 137/137, lint exit 0.

=== NON-BLOCKING ===
F. [MEDIUM, follow-up] TOCTOU between the SSRF check and the connection. assertHostIsSafe resolves DNS; fetchImpl then resolves DNS again on its own. A rebinding resolver (short TTL, answers public then private) passes the check and connects privately. Requirement 10 as written is met — this is the known limitation of check-then-fetch. Real fix is connection pinning (an undici Agent whose connect.lookup returns the vetted address, or fetch-by-IP with a Host header), which is bigger than this sprint and touches how Sprint 5 constructs fetchImpl. Record it for Master Controller; don't let it be forgotten because "req 10 says after DNS resolution and we did that."
G. [LOW] classify.js:67 matchesKeyword uses startsWith for BOTH lists. Exclusion by prefix is the wrong direction: 'tagline-sitemap.xml' → excluded (tag), 'authority-sitemap.xml' → excluded (author). Unrealistic names, but requirement 6 says unsure → include, and prefix-exclusion is unsure → exclude. Exclusion should be exact-token; inclusion can stay loose.
H. [LOW] httpClient.js:73 compares hostname only when deciding to forward Authorization on redirect. An https→http redirect on the same host still sends Basic credentials in cleartext. Compare origin (scheme+host+port), or at least refuse the downgrade.
I. [LOW] URLs carrying userinfo (https://u:p@host/) are echoed into error messages and the attempts log verbatim. Strip userinfo from URLs before they go into error text, or reject userinfo URLs up front — Sprint 2's validator already drops it on save, so this only reaches via manualSitemapUrl.

=== RULING ON THE DESIGN QUESTION (requirement 7 / Sprint 5 contract) ===
Q: Plaintext {username, password} boundary vs. importing and calling Sprint 2's decrypt helper inside the module.
A: The plaintext boundary is correct. Keep it. Reasons: (1) The requirement's operative clause is "rather than reimplementing decryption" — the module reimplements nothing; it never sees ciphertext. (2) The Dependencies line explicitly authorizes "code against a narrow interface and integrate when it does"; a plaintext credential pair IS the narrow interface. (3) Sprint 2's helper is repository.getDecryptedBasicAuthPassword(id) — it needs an open DB handle and a project id. Importing that into lib/sitemap would couple the crawl engine to SQLite and to project identity, which is the wrong layer and would break the fixture-only test property requirement 13 demands. (4) The acceptance criterion "imports nothing from Sprint 2's route layer — only its decrypt helper" is satisfied in the only sensible reading: the module imports nothing from Sprint 2 at all, and the decrypt helper is consumed by the caller.
INTEGRATION CONTRACT FOR SPRINT 5, on the record: the scan route calls repository.getDecryptedBasicAuthPassword(projectId) (Sprint 2, the ONLY decrypt path), builds { username: project.basicAuthUsername, password: <that> }, passes it as options.auth to discoverAndParseSitemap, and never persists, logs, or renders the plaintext. Sprint 5's QA1 audit will check exactly that.

=== FOR THE RE-AUDIT ===
Five required fixes, all inside lib/sitemap/ (crawl.js, ssrf.js, httpClient.js, xml.js) plus tests. Keep it to that and the re-audit is: re-run the five demonstrations above (flat-index budget, maxChildren:1, truncated-child recording, bracketed literal in both spellings through guardedFetch, valid body + text/html), re-run the offline-stubbed suite, re-verify the tree. I will not re-derive the rest unless the diff reaches it.
Note for Pipeman/LiveQA when this eventually ships: per the sprint file, LiveQA's check on this sprint is a boot + existing-screens smoke test only; the engine gets its live verification in Sprint 5.

PASS: QA1 STATIC AUDIT — SPRINT 3 — ROUND 2 (RE-AUDIT) — VERDICT: PASS
Audited commit f6a3cfed04e885783f491953e4462267de47f565 on devteam2/sprint-3 in worktree ../content-checker-devteam2-sprint-3. Worktree clean; committed code. Verdict recorded from the worktree, where this sprint's lifecycle state lives.
Sprint file: byte-identical to the copy read fresh at round 1 of this session (git diff 786dcb5..f6a3cfe on docs/sprints/2-in-progress/ is empty). No cross-version criterion applies. Requirements unchanged; this round is focused on what moved. Round-1 findings on the rest of the module stand as recorded.

SCOPE — slightly wider than the four files I named, and correctly so: lib/sitemap/{crawl,index,errors,httpClient,ssrf,xml}.js plus five test files. index.js needed the budget-wide AbortController; errors.js needed BudgetExceededError so an in-flight budget abort is typed distinctly from a per-request TIMEOUT. Ownership boundary held (nothing outside lib/sitemap, test/sitemap, lifecycle bookkeeping). No new dependencies this round.

THE FIVE REQUIRED FIXES — ALL RESOLVED, EACH DEMONSTRATED BY RE-RUNNING THE ROUND-1 PROBE UNCHANGED
A. Overall budget across queued siblings — CLOSED. Same probe as round 1 (10-child flat index, concurrency 1, 30ms each, budgetMs 50): round 1 fetched 10/10 in 319ms with truncated:false; now fetches 2/10 in 52ms with truncated:true. Mechanism: one AbortController per discoverAndParseSitemap call, started BEFORE discovery, combined into every fetch via AbortSignal.any; guardedFetch also checks the signal at entry and at each redirect hop. In-flight cut-off verified separately: a single child whose fetch takes 200ms under a 50ms budget returns at 51ms with skipped:[{reason:'truncated:budget'}] — typed as a budget abort, not mistaken for a per-request TIMEOUT. Discovery is now inside the budget too (round-1 note I).
B. Root counted against the child cap — CLOSED. maxChildren:1 now fetches exactly 1 child (round 1: zero). Cap/budget check and increment moved inside the !parsedDoc branch; a pre-parsed root never touches it.
C. Truncated children unrecorded / ambiguous flagged pre-visit — CLOSED. Truncated children land in skipped with 'truncated:cap' | 'truncated:budget' (seen in the in-flight probe above). The ambiguous push moved to after the visit and is gated on ctx.consulted.includes(child), so a child that was cut off cannot appear as "included, check it." index.js JSDoc updated to enumerate every skipped reason for Sprint 5.
D. SSRF: hex-spelled IPv4-mapped hole + bracketed-literal DNS bug — CLOSED, both together as required. ssrf.js rewritten on net.BlockList (mirrors Sprint 2's fix independently, no import), with the correct extras kept (0.0.0.0/8, ::, fe80::/10, fc00::/7). Literal IPs are bracket-stripped and checked directly with no DNS round trip. Unit matrix: ::ffff:7f00:1 and ::ffff:c0a8:10a now BLOCK (round 1: ALLOW); ::ffff:8.8.8.8, ::ffff:808:808, 2001:4860:4860::8888, 172.32.0.1 still allow (no over-blocking). Through guardedFetch with the REAL resolver: http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/, http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/, http://[::1]/ all SSRF_BLOCKED (round 1: DNS_ERROR — wrong type). A legitimate http://[2001:db8::1]/sitemap.xml now fetches (round 1: DNS_ERROR).
E. Content-type veto on a valid body — CLOSED. Valid <urlset> with contentType text/html now parses. Content-type is consulted only after XMLValidator has already rejected the body, and then only to choose NON_XML_RESPONSE over MALFORMED_XML. Comment and code now agree.

TESTS AND TOOLCHAIN
Full suite 158/158, lint exit 0. Sitemap suite re-run with dns.lookup, dns.promises.lookup, resolve4/6 and global fetch replaced by throwing stubs: 121/121 — still fixture-only. New tests include the exact flat-index-budget and bracketed-literal-both-spellings cases from round 1, going through the real path.

ONE NEW NON-BLOCKING ITEM FOUND THIS ROUND
J. [LOW] Duplicate ambiguous entries when the same unclassifiable child is referenced from two parents and the second reference arrives after the first has completed. DEMONSTRATED: root → gallery-sitemap.xml directly, and root → post-sitemap.xml (delayed 30ms) → gallery-sitemap.xml; result.ambiguous lists gallery-sitemap.xml twice. Fetched once, urls correct — purely a duplicate in the advisory list, so Sprint 5's UI would show the same "check this" line twice. Fix is a Set on ambiguous URLs, or pushing ambiguous from inside visitSitemap on first consult only. Fold into any later touch of crawl.js.

NON-BLOCKING ITEMS CARRIED FROM ROUND 1 — unchanged, still open, none required for ship
F. [MEDIUM, for Master Controller] TOCTOU between the SSRF check's DNS resolution and fetch's own. Requirement 10 is met as written; connection pinning (undici Agent with a vetted lookup, or fetch-by-IP + Host header) is the real fix and should be scoped as its own item, likely alongside Sprint 5 when fetchImpl's construction is decided.
G. [LOW] classify.js exclusion list matches by prefix; exclusion should be exact-token.
H. [LOW] Same-host https→http redirect still forwards Basic auth; compare origin, not hostname.
I. [LOW] userinfo in a manualSitemapUrl is echoed into error text and the attempts log.

RULING FROM ROUND 1 STANDS: plaintext {username, password} boundary is the correct design; Sprint 5's route calls repository.getDecryptedBasicAuthPassword(id) and passes the result in. Sprint 5's audit will check that.

FOR PIPEMAN / LIVEQA
Per the sprint file, LiveQA's check on this sprint is a boot + existing-screens smoke test only (no UI was added; nothing in src/ changed). The engine's live verification belongs to Sprint 5. This branch is off 11bca26 (Sprint 1 close) and main has since taken Sprint 2 — Pipeman's merge/rebase will change the SHA but not the audited tree content unless there's a conflict; there should be none (disjoint files, package.json/lockfile both add one dependency in different places). If the merge does touch a file in lib/sitemap or test/sitemap, that's a content change and /sprint-ship will refuse — re-audit rather than force.

PASS: QA1 STATIC AUDIT — SPRINT 3 — ROUND 3 (MERGE RE-AUDIT, triggered by /sprint-ship's tree-hash refusal) — VERDICT: PASS
Audited commit 39da8b7739952b8b2973728d4b96a051e50c306d on main (merge of devteam2/sprint-3 @ f6a3cfe into main @ 365da6f, --no-ff). Working tree clean; committed. Verdict recorded from main, where the sprint's state now lives.
Sprint file re-read fresh: byte-identical to the copy audited in rounds 1-2 (sha256 caa5049b..., matching the recorded qa1_audit_file_hash). No cross-version criterion applies.

WHY THIS ROUND EXISTS — and a correction to my own round-2 note
Pipeman ran /sprint-ship 3 and the tool refused: the merge commit's tree hash differs from the one recorded at round 2. Pipeman read the script rather than trusting the handoffs and is correct: qa1_audited_tree_hash is the WHOLE-REPO tree (git rev-parse <commit>^{tree}), not path-scoped. My round-2 handoff said the merge would "change the SHA but not the audited tree content" if it stayed off lib/sitemap — that was wrong; I asserted the check's scope without reading it. A merge that combines Sprint 2 (on main since 365da6f) with Sprint 3 (branched from 11bca26, before Sprint 2) necessarily has a different whole-repo tree than either parent, no matter how clean the merge. The refusal is the check working exactly as designed, and this re-audit is the documented recovery path (cmd_qa1 accepts dev_agreed_done). Pipeman also correctly carried the worktree's uncommitted state file (round-2 PASS, dev_agreed_done) into the merge rather than shipping a history that claimed dev_build.
FOR WHOEVER OWNS THE TOOLING: this will recur on every Dev Team 2 worktree sprint whenever main moves in the meantime. It is not a bug — an unaudited merge is exactly what the hash exists to catch — but the recovery path could be cheaper: QA1 could audit the merge commit rather than the branch tip when a worktree sprint is ready to ship. Master Controller's call.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED — the merge is the exact union of two already-audited trees, proven four ways
1. git diff f6a3cfe 39da8b7 -- lib/sitemap test/sitemap test/fixtures/sitemap → EMPTY. Sprint 3's audited files are byte-identical to the round-2 PASS.
2. git diff --name-status 365da6f 39da8b7, excluding Sprint 3's pure additions → only: the sprint-3 file moved 1-todo → 2-in-progress (R100, content identical), registry.json, state/sprint-3.json (bookkeeping), package.json, package-lock.json.
3. package.json: exactly one added line ("fast-xml-parser": "^5.11.1"). package-lock.json: eight node_modules entries ADDED (fast-xml-parser and its transitive deps, the same set as round 1), NOTHING removed — Sprint 2's dependency set is intact.
4. git diff 365da6f 39da8b7 -- src/ views/ test/db test/lib test/middleware test/routes test/*.test.js bin/ public/ .env.example .gitignore → EMPTY. Sprint 2's shipped, audited files are untouched.
So: nothing in this commit is code QA1 has not already audited and passed. What is new is the COMBINATION, so the combination is what I tested:
- Full suite on the merged tree, run by me: 239/239, lint exit 0.
- Sitemap suite with dns.lookup/resolve4/resolve6/global fetch stubbed to throw: 121/121 — still fixture-only after the merge.
- Boot check with Sprint 2's config surface (SESSION_SECRET, TEAM_PASSWORD_HASH, ENCRYPTION_KEY) and Sprint 3's module loaded in the same process: /healthz 200, discoverAndParseSitemap resolves to a function. The two sprints coexist.

VERDICT RATIONALE
Content already audited + combination verified working = PASS. No new findings. Round-2's non-blocking items (F connection-pinning for MC; G/H/I; J duplicate-ambiguous) carry forward unchanged and are not re-listed here — see round 2.

NEXT
This PASS records the merge commit's tree hash. Dev Team 2 runs /sprint-dev-done 3 (from main now, where the state lives), then Pipeman ships 39da8b7. Per the sprint file, LiveQA's check is a boot + existing-screens smoke test; the engine's live verification is Sprint 5's.
